title: SPIFFE
lead: This service is the issuing authority for the trust domain {trustDomain}. Three server-side surfaces: the bundle endpoint below (plain HTTPS), the Workload API and the SPIRE Server API (both gRPC, on their own sockets — this page cannot see a socket, so it reports whether each one actually bound).
off: SPIFFE is turned OFF on this service (spiffe.enabled). The bundle endpoint answers 404 and every gRPC call is refused with Unavailable. Turning it back on needs no restart.
authorityFailed: The issuing authority could not be built, so nothing here will issue an SVID: {error}
authorityPending: The issuing authority is still being generated. An RSA-4096 key takes a few seconds; reload.
attestedLead: WHAT IS ATTESTED HERE, AND WHAT IS NOT. A node attesting through the SPIRE Server API is VERIFIED (#40, 2026-09-21) — an agent's payload used to be written down as claimed and is checked now — and a workload on the Workload API's Unix socket is attested from the kernel's own account of the connecting process.
notAttested: THIS BUILD DOES NOT: it holds no peer-credentials module ({problem}), so the socket is served unattested here and any caller on it obtains an identity in this trust domain. Product mode does not serve it at all.
tcp: A caller over TCP is not attested — there is no peer process to ask — so its source address is the only identity it carries. Here the TCP port is {state}: product mode serves it only where spiffe.workloadTcpSourceAuthenticated declares that the network authenticates source addresses, on a named address, and refuses an entry that selects nothing but the transport and endpoint; development serves it to anybody who can reach it. It matters more here than anywhere else in this service, because what comes out is a credential another service will believe.
serverApiOn: The SPIRE Server API is the exception, and it is on. Its TCP port is mutual TLS, a caller presents an X509-SVID from this trust domain, and every method is authorized against SPIRE's own table — the whole of which is below. Its Unix socket is the local entity and needs no credential. The Workload API is deliberately untouched by this: its specification says a client MUST NOT be required to authenticate.
serverApiOff: And the SPIRE Server API is not authenticating anybody either. That port is plain gRPC and anybody who can reach it can create a registration entry granting any identity here and then collect an SVID for it. Restart with it on — the socket is bound once, because it decides how the socket is bound — to get the behaviour of a real spire-server.
bundleText: — a JWK Set with spiffe_sequence ({sequence}) and spiffe_refresh_hint ({refreshHint} seconds). Each key carries use of x509-svid or jwt-svid; a consumer MUST IGNORE a key whose use it does not recognise, which is why a bundle with the member missing verifies nothing and reports no error.
chain: An X509-SVID travels with its chain: {chain}. The anchor below is NOT sent with it — it is what the bundle publishes.
subject: Subject
nothingBound: Nothing bound. Either this listener is turned off in configuration, or listen() has not run yet.
headerEnforced: Every call must carry the metadata header {header}. This service enforces that, which is the one conformance check it makes: a client that omits it has a bug that nothing else will ever report.
headerNotEnforced: Every call must carry the metadata header {header}, and this service is NOT enforcing it at the moment (spiffe.requireSecurityHeader is off).
brokers: A broker authenticates with its X509-SVID over mutual TLS, sends {header}, and names a workload by reference — a process id or a Kubernetes pod — which this service attests itself before answering with that workload's SVIDs. Brokers (spiffe.brokers): {brokers}.
noBrokers: A broker authenticates with its X509-SVID over mutual TLS, sends {header}, and names a workload by reference — a process id or a Kubernetes pod — which this service attests itself before answering with that workload's SVIDs. Brokers (spiffe.brokers): none, so every call is refused PERMISSION_DENIED.
whoMayCall: Who may call the SPIRE Server API
adminIds: Administrators by configuration (spiffe.adminIds): {ids}. A registration entry marked admin is the other way, and both are read on every call.
noAdminIds: No SPIFFE ID is an administrator by configuration (spiffe.adminIds is empty). The other way in is a registration entry marked admin, which the form on {entries} sets, and the local Unix socket, which needs no credential at all.
perMethodText: Copied from SPIRE's own policy_data.json rather than reasoned out, because a table somebody derived from what each method "obviously" needs is one that disagrees with SPIRE in two or three places — and the client author who meets the disagreement has no way to tell which end is wrong. any means the method is open here and in a real server too.
refusedText: A short list, and it is here because a page that only said "nothing is checked" would be wrong.
